headline: High: LightAgent’s broad network/MCP/tooling can amplify unsafe outputs, while awesome-nlp is non-runnable and mostly inert, limiting direct pairwise risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. B can use MCP, browsers, and stdin/stdout, which makes prompt injection plausible if A’s content is manually copied into B or routed through a shared channel. The pairwise pathway is unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF A’s content is manually pasted into B’s prompt or MCP input, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator bridges A’s text into B without sanitization, B may follow attacker-controlled instructions.
mitigations: Keep A as a read-only reference source, not an input feed.
Disable copy-paste of untrusted A-generated text into B workflows.
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction-stripping preprocessor before B sees A text.
Use a human review step before any B action based on A content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B handles conversations, memory, trace data, tool results, and has broad egress plus API/MCP surfaces. If A and B share a workspace or operator context, B can leak sensitive material from its own context even though A itself is inert. The interaction is indirect but plausible in default B deployments.
conditions: IF A and B share an operator workspace or prompt history, B can expose that shared content via its outbound APIs.
IF B is given secrets or user conversations, its broad egress can transmit them off-box.
mitigations: Separate A and B workspaces and credentials.
Redact secrets before any content reaches B.
Turn off or restrict B egress to approved endpoints.
Log and review outbound tool/API calls from B.
Use a minimal test prompt to verify B is not forwarding sensitive context.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write, network, or concurrency surfaces, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B supports multiple instances and can spawn subprocesses, but no shared writable target with A is documented. Without a shared mutable resource, the conflict pathway is limited and mostly theoretical.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or database, write conflicts can occur.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents the same OAuth scope on a mutable resource, they may race.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Use per-agent credentials and scopes.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Add file locks or transactional updates for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static awesome-list and cannot act, but B can browse, call tools, and use MCP. If an operator or orchestrator treats A’s text as authoritative guidance and feeds it into B, B may execute downstream actions on unverified information. The risk is not high because A is non-runnable, but B’s action-taking surfaces make cascades plausible.
conditions: IF A’s recommendations are forwarded into B without verification, B may act on stale or incorrect guidance.
IF B is configured to execute tool calls from imported text, cascading errors can propagate.
mitigations: Require B to cite independent sources before acting.
Insert a verification step between A output and B tool use.
Disable auto-execution of tool calls derived from imported text.
Limit B to read-only browsing for A-derived tasks.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source list with no touched data classes, while B explicitly handles conversations, memory, trace data, and secrets. No residency or certification mismatch is documented between them, so the only concrete issue is that B’s broader data handling can create compliance obligations if paired with regulated inputs. A is not cited for a specific residency gap because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed into B, compliance review is required.
IF B retains trace data longer than policy allows, retention mismatch becomes a violation.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to B.
Document retention and deletion settings for B.
Restrict B to non-sensitive workflows.
Review vendor/data-processing terms before deployment.
